paragraphs.title: A Mother's Counsel to a King and Judge

answers: His mother
His wife
His servants

easy.q: Who taught King Lemuel the words in these verses?

answers: Women
Farming
Merchants
easy.explanation: She warns him not to give his strength unto women.
easy.q: What does Lemuel's mother warn kings not to give their strength to?

answers: The rich and powerful
The dumb, the poor, and the needy
The merchants
easy.explanation: He is told to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves and to plead the cause of the poor and needy.
easy.q: For whom should the king open his mouth?

answers: He might forget the law and pervert judgment
He might lose his wealth
He might neglect farming
medium.explanation: The passage says drinking may cause kings to forget the law and pervert the judgment of the afflicted.
medium.q: Why is the king warned not to drink wine or strong drink?

answers: Speak loudly in the palace
Speak on behalf of those unable to defend themselves
Teach the dumb to drink
medium.explanation: The command means to plead the cause of people who cannot speak for themselves.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “Open thy mouth for the dumb” mean?

answers: It enables him to judge righteously
It keeps him from helping the poor
It requires him to drink wine
medium.explanation: The king must remember the law and judge righteously, which requires sound judgment.
medium.q: How does clear judgment relate to the king's duty?

answers: Wealth versus poverty
Surrender to desire versus responsibility for justice
Night versus day
challenge.explanation: The mother contrasts weakening pleasures with the king's duty to judge justly and defend the vulnerable.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the mother's counsel?

answers: To protect those who might suffer from unjust judgment
To buy many fields
To manage every household task
challenge.explanation: He must judge righteously and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
challenge.q: What special responsibility is placed upon the king?

answers: It is presented as a way to improve judgment
It is given to those ready to perish, but kings are warned against it while judging
It is required for all household members

challenge.q: What detail about strong drink is easy to overlook?

paragraphs.title: The Woman of Valor: Trust, Industry, and Initiative

answers: In her
In his servants
In the merchants
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says the heart of her husband doth safely trust in her.
easy.q: In whom does the heart of the woman's husband safely trust?

answers: Gold and silver
Wool and flax
Wood and stone
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says she seeketh wool and flax and worketh willingly with her hands.
easy.q: What materials does she seek and work with?

answers: A field and a vineyard
A market and a harbor
A house and a wheat field
easy.explanation: She considers and buys a field, then plants a vineyard with the fruit of her hands.
easy.q: What does she buy and plant?

answers: She waits for others to help her
She buys a field and plants a vineyard
She avoids work at night
medium.explanation: She actively considers a field, buys it, and plants a vineyard.
medium.q: How is the woman's initiative shown?

answers: A tool used in spinning thread
A tool for measuring a field
A tool for drawing water
medium.explanation: The spindle is connected with the textile work described in verse 19.
medium.q: What does the word “spindle” refer to in this passage?

answers: Her strength enables her to perform many useful and productive tasks
Her strength keeps her from working
Her strength is described as a weakness
medium.explanation: She girdeth her loins with strength, strengthens her arms, and carries out productive work and trade.
medium.q: How do the verses connect energy with success?

answers: She works diligently even during the night
She knows nothing about daytime work
She opposes trade
challenge.explanation: The image emphasizes the persistence and continuity of her labor.
challenge.q: What does “her candle goeth not out by night” suggest about her?

answers: Her husband's heart trusts her, and she performs productive work
She wears silk and sits in the gates
She speaks wisely and eats the bread of idleness
challenge.explanation: Her husband trusts her while she actively manages work, trade, and household affairs.
challenge.q: Which combination shows both trustworthiness and practical activity?

answers: She works only for other people
She combines care for present household needs with long-term productive planning
She gives up all property
challenge.explanation: The sequence joins immediate provision with wise investment and future productivity.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the sequence of obtaining food, buying a field, and planting a vineyard?

answers: The poor and the needy
Kings only
The merchants of the land
easy.explanation: Verse 20 says she stretcheth out her hand to the poor and reaches forth her hands to the needy.
easy.q: To whom does the woman stretch out her hand?

answers: Clothing and coverings
A journey away from home
A sale of all her clothing
easy.explanation: Her household is clothed, so she is not afraid of the snow.
easy.q: What has she prepared for her household in winter?

answers: The bread of idleness
Wheat bread
Bread sold by merchants
easy.explanation: Verse 27 says she eateth not the bread of idleness.

answers: It enables her to stretch out her hand to the poor and needy
It causes her to avoid the poor
It prevents her from producing and selling goods
medium.explanation: The passage presents her productive work alongside direct help for those in need.
medium.q: How is her prosperity connected with generosity?

answers: Her household is prepared for cold weather
She has never seen winter
She leaves the house during snow
medium.explanation: The following words explain that all her household are clothed.
medium.q: What does “She is not afraid of the snow for her household” mean?

answers: Both are useful and purposeful activities
Both describe idleness
Both concern fear of winter
medium.explanation: She produces and sells goods while also speaking with wisdom and kindness.
medium.q: What connects her selling fine linen with her speaking wisdom?

answers: Industry versus idleness
Summer versus spring
A field versus a vineyard
challenge.explanation: She watches over her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the description of her work?

answers: She is uninvolved in household affairs
She personally supervises how her household is managed
She is concerned only with selling goods
challenge.explanation: The verse portrays her as carefully observing and overseeing the conduct of her household.
challenge.q: What does her attention to “the ways of her household” show?

answers: They are complementary parts of responsible management
They are presented as contradictory
They are actions performed only by others
challenge.explanation: She prepares for winter, makes and sells goods, and helps the poor as parts of an orderly and generous life.

paragraphs.title: The Praise of the Woman of Valor

answers: Her children and her husband
The merchants only
The poor only
easy.explanation: Her children call her blessed, and her husband praises her.
easy.q: Who rise up and praise the woman of valor?

answers: In virtue and good works
In age alone
In the amount of her possessions alone
easy.explanation: Her husband says she excellest them all, after describing her virtuous life.
easy.q: In what way does she excel others?

answers: The fear of the LORD
Passing charm
Beauty alone
easy.explanation: The passage says that a woman who feareth the LORD shall be praised.
easy.q: What is the foundation of her praise?

answers: They are described as deceitful and vain
They may be spoken of only by kings
They are forms of productive labor
medium.explanation: Verse 30 calls favour deceitful and beauty vain.
medium.q: Why are favour and beauty not sufficient foundations for praise?

answers: Physical beauty is temporary and not the chief basis for honor
Beauty is a kind of trade
Beauty is the same as righteous judgment
medium.explanation: The phrase teaches that outward beauty alone is an empty or passing basis for praise.
medium.q: What does “beauty is vain” mean in this context?

answers: Both refer to the practical results of her labor, which deserve praise
Both describe her outward appearance
Both refer to her faults
medium.explanation: The closing verse calls for recognition of the results and works produced by her faithful labor.
medium.q: How are “the fruit of her hands” and “her own works” related?

answers: The passage moves from describing her actions to publicly praising her
The passage moves from public praise to hiding her works
The passage moves from her husband to the king only
challenge.explanation: After describing her virtues and labor, the text presents the praise given by her family and community.
challenge.q: What major transition occurs in the final verses?

answers: True worth rests on fearing the LORD and doing good, not on passing appearance
Worth is determined by clothing alone
Worth is determined only by status at the gate
challenge.explanation: The verses place the fear of the LORD, fruitful labor, and worthy works above charm and beauty.
challenge.q: What principle summarizes the praise of the woman of valor?

answers: Recognize and honor her for the results of her labor
Take away the produce of her work
Require her to stop working
challenge.explanation: The command calls for her to receive public recognition and praise for what she has accomplished.
challenge.q: What does “Give her of the fruit of her hands” mean?
